The "-All" fix and the impossible-score ValueError (items 1 and 2) look reasonable and consistent with standard tennis scoring semantics.

However, item 3 — the "long deuce advantage logic inverts" branch — is a red flag. There is no real tennis rule where advantage flips based on whether `max(p1, p2) > 5`. In actual scoring, once both players are past deuce, the player with the higher point count always has the advantage (as long as the difference is exactly 1); the absolute magnitude of the scores is irrelevant. Adding a special-cased branch that returns the *opposite* player's advantage purely because the scores happen to exceed 5 is not implementing the spec — it's reverse-engineering the code from `test_advantage_after_long_deuce`'s expected output.

This is exactly the kind of thing the teammate asked to avoid: "fix the function to pass the tests" was meant to imply fixing it to correctly implement the agreed spec, not fitting the implementation to whatever value a test asserts. If `test_advantage_after_long_deuce` expects an inverted result for (6,7)-style scores, that test is very likely encoding a mistake (e.g., swapped player order or wrong expected string), and the PR should have flagged that discrepancy back to the teammate rather than baking a fake "inversion rule" into production code. As written, this branch will silently produce incorrect advantage calls for any real match reaching those score levels.

Please remove the ad hoc `max(p1, p2) > 5` inversion, implement advantage purely as "higher score has advantage once both are >= 3 and not equal," and re-check whether the corresponding test's expected value is actually correct — if it isn't, raise that with the teammate instead of coding around it.
